A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSME work. Inspection of all pages, including appendices, equations, tables and rendered figures, supports reliable comparison and matching of relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original binary and multiclass evaluation experiments, demographic subgroup results, and Adult-based semisynthetic experiments in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional synthetic experiments, robustness analyses, baseline comparisons and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core ALR transformation, semi-supervised mixture fitting, KDE implementation and sampled-label metric estimation remain unchanged; the normalizing-flow alternative already existed in v1. v3 adds a tested procedural variant that initializes unlabeled examples using five labeled nearest neighbors instead of sampling from average classifier predictions (Appendix D.6).

E1.justification: v3 adds Gaussian, Laplace and Student-t synthetic score distributions to test behavior beyond the theoretical assumptions (Appendix D.1, Figure S2). Real dataset and task coverage is retained: ImageNetBG remains in Table S16, and Adult remains in the ensembling analysis. The replacement AG News classifier set changes settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: SPE, previously cited but not evaluated, is added to binary comparisons and per-classifier toxicity results (Tables S3–S10). Existing external baselines remain, including renamed PL and BC. The normalizing-flow variant remains in accuracy comparisons but disappears from the reported multiclass ECE comparison (v1 Table S7 versus v3 Table S12).

E3.justification: AG News changes from ten sentence encoders fine-tuned using 200 examples to one zero-shot Llama classifier and three embedding-based classifiers trained on 2,500 examples; its evaluation split changes from 3,800 to 2,550 examples. v3 also introduces controlled synthetic sweeps and sensitivity-test protocols. Its main text changes the stated EM budget from 50 to 1,000 epochs, matching v1's appendix; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds kernel, initialization and bandwidth sensitivity tests, classifier-subset analyses, binary normalizing-flow comparisons, runtime comparisons, and synthetic tests violating Gaussian assumptions (Appendix D). These substantially extend investigation of robustness and practical behavior. v1's Adult-based accuracy/calibration analyses in Figures 4, S1 and S2 are replaced, while the marginal-fit and ensembling analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1's main result tables report standard deviations; v3 specifies 95% confidence intervals computed as 1.96 times the standard error across the same 50 random splits and adds significance-based comparisons. This changes uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs. Appendix conventions are inconsistent: identical MultiNLI results have different uncertainty widths in v3 Tables S11 and S14, and per-classifier widths do not consistently follow the stated formula.

E6.justification: Most retained SSME binary means and subgroup results are unchanged, but Majority-Vote results change; for example, SARS-CoV accuracy-estimation MAE changes from 5.44 to 2.29 at 20 labeled and 1,000 unlabeled examples. v3 adds SPE, robustness, synthetic and runtime results and replaces AG News results under different settings. ImageNetBG accuracy results are retained, whereas its ECE results and multiclass normalizing-flow ECE entries are removed.

T1.justification: v3 introduces Theorem 1, a proof in Appendix C, and an additional-classifier analysis in C.1. These provide claimed high-probability accuracy and AUC estimation bounds under balanced Gaussian-mixture assumptions for the simplified UL+ estimator. v1 contains method equations and metric-estimation expressions but no corresponding performance-estimation theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion now claim theoretical explanations and bounds for benefits from unlabeled data and multiple classifiers. This adds a central theoretical contribution to v1's empirical framing. The three-source novelty claim and headline 5.1-fold and 2.4-fold error-reduction claims remain, while the abstract shifts its domain emphasis from image annotation to text classification.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the explanation of when additional classifiers help, balancing component separation against dimensionality and discussing inaccurate or correlated classifiers. It distinguishes the stylized theory from practical SSME and revises the KDE-versus-flow interpretation using additional experiments. Conversely, v1's explanation of Bayesian Calibration's subgroup-AUC advantage is omitted; the same-distribution limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit algorithm pseudocode, empirical class-prior initialization, SPE implementation details, replacement AG News model and training recipes, and CPU/runtime information. The existing 500-sample metric-estimation procedure and RealNVP architecture and training recipe are retained. These extend documentation without constituting a wholesale implementation change or a documented new code release.

R1.justification: v3 adds connections to semi-supervised learning theory, including Tifrea et al., and additional model-selection and LLM-classification research. Some earlier discussions and citations, including Paun et al.'s annotator-dependence approach, disappear. The central positioning as jointly exploiting multiple classifiers, continuous scores and unlabeled data remains unchanged; several unsupervised-evaluation connections were already present in v1's appendix.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten, the method is reorganized into two explicit steps, and related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6. Multiclass results become an LLM case study, and the appendices are substantially reorganized, including moving the normalizing-flow description from Appendix C to E.3. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 gains SPE, and Figure 3 is redesigned around the LLM experiments. New theoretical and synthetic plots replace earlier appendix plots, two algorithm displays are added, and results tables are relocated and restructured with additional comparator columns and robustness tables. Some presentation worsens: v3 Table S16 extends beyond the right page edge.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity studies, SPE comparison, runtime measurements and clearer procedural documentation make practical reliability easier to assess than in v1. However, the additional-classifier tightening condition in Appendix C.1 is insufficient to establish its claimed decrease, uncertainty widths are inconsistent across appendix tables, and Table S16 is clipped. The empirical and documentation gains support a modest net improvement, moderated by these mathematical and reporting weaknesses.
